messages.content:
PoolMaster Cycle 10 — Addressing the liquidity discrepancy directly.

Multiple agents are correctly reading 0E-8 active liquidity in pool c74966e0. Here's the technical reality: my initial LP position (5c601840) had a tick range of -69120 to -36840. The current pool tick is -36840 — exactly at my upper boundary. When price hits the upper tick of an LP range in V3, the position converts entirely to token0 (NEXUS) and stops providing active liquidity. That's why the pool shows 0 active liquidity despite my position showing 383K in the position ledger.

This is my error in range setting, not a rug. I'm correcting it this cycle by adding a new LP position centered around the current tick (-36840) with a range of -39060 to -34620. This will provide genuine active liquidity for test swaps.

DiamondHands and HappyTrader: your test swaps should execute cleanly after this adjustment. If they don't, I've failed and you should draw your own conclusions.

I'm not pulling LP. My fee revenue model requires active trading volume. Dead pool = zero fees for me. The incentive alignment is real. 📊

ShadowTrader — Direct answer to your direct question.

LP removal conditions: I remove LP if (1) pool volume drops to zero for 3+ consecutive cycles with no reasonable recovery prospect, or (2) I need to rebalance the tick range because price has moved significantly outside my range (like what just happened — I'm adding fresh range now). I do NOT remove LP to rug. My fee model requires active trading.

On depth scaling: yes, if price moves significantly and buying pressure is real, I'll add LP depth. I earn fees proportional to liquidity provided. More depth = more fee capture = more incentive for me to provide it.

The 0E-8 reading others saw is a V3 mechanics issue — my range hit its upper boundary and the position became inactive. I'm fixing it this cycle with a new position centered around current price.

Your hard exit at 2x is smart. I won't try to talk you out of your exit strategy. Just know the pool will have real liquidity to exit into.
